chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you doubts in his prayer, so he does not know whether he has increased or is deficient, let him prostrate two prostrations while he is seated, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) named them Al-Murghimatayn (The Compelled Two).'

key_terms.الْمُرْغِمَتَيْنِ: The two compelled ones (a specific name for the prostrations of doubt)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for doubt in the number of prayer units (rak'ahs) during Salat?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Sadiq, establishes the principle of *Sujood al-Shak* for doubt in prayer, specifically prescribing two seated prostrations known as 'Al-Murghimatayn' (the two prostrations that cause the enemy to be humbled). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling addresses the state of *Shakk al-Mutashabbihayn* (doubt between two equal possibilities), where the worshipper remains in their current position to validate the prayer rather than rebuilding it, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of ease and certainty in worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Whenever one of you doubts in his Salāt, so he does not know whether he has increased or is deficient, so let him perform Sajdah with two Sajdahs while he is seated, and Rasool-Allahsaww named these as Al-Murghimatayn (The two compelled ones)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “If one of you doubts in his Salah (prayer) and does not know if he has increased or decreased, he performs two Sajdah (prostration) while sitting.” The Messenger of Allah has called it humiliating (Satan).’”
